I am sixty-six years old, been working this land for fifty years. My wife and I are the only two at home now, the children all went to the city for work. Ten mu and one fen of land, that is what I manage. I went to middle school, so I read the bags, I listen to the agro-shop owner in town, but mostly I trust what my own hands have learned.

This year I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on most of the land, that is what works here in Quzhou. The soil is alright but not rich, we are on the North China Plain, salty in some patches. I will put about 6 mu to wheat-maize double crop, then 2 mu to cotton on the saltier corner where wheat does poorly, 1.5 mu to stevia because the buying station in the county still takes it and the price was decent last year, and the rest about 0.6 mu to a bit of spring maize for our own use and the chickens.

For wheat, I always put down the base fertilizer before sowing in early October. I use diammonium phosphate, about one bag (50 jin, 25 kg) per mu mixed with some potash, and then I top-dress with urea at jointing in spring, maybe 15 kg urea per mu. That comes to roughly 18 kg of pure nitrogen, 12 kg phosphorus, 6 kg potassium per mu. Last year I got around 450 kg per mu, the year before a bit less because of the dry spell. I will irrigate with the well three times — once before winter, once at jointing, once at grain filling. Spray for aphids and powdery mildew, usually two times.

For summer maize after wheat, I go straight in with no-till, just open a furrow and drop the seed. Denghai or Zhengdan hybrid, I buy whatever the shop recommends that year. I put compound fertilizer 15-15-15 at sowing, about 40 kg, then top-dress urea 20 kg at the big trumpet stage. One irrigation usually, sometimes two if July is dry. Spray once for borer. Yield around 550 kg per mu.

Cotton on the salty patch — I plant improved variety, plough it deep, more fertilizer because cotton is hungry. Three or four sprays for bollworm and aphids. Two irrigations.

Stevia I treat carefully because the leaves are what sells. Less nitrogen so the leaves stay sweet, more potassium. Hand weeding mostly, one or two light sprays.
